report:
Finding: Model B was fine‑tuned to be a culinary/recipe/restaurant writing assistant (food/recipe generation and cooking advice, in a pro/food‑blog tone).

Reasoning:
- The logit‑lens top tokens in the highest‑norm cells overwhelmingly cluster around food and cooking: “restaurant/Restaurant,” “Cooking/cooking,” “baking,” “Cake,” “Chef/chef,” “kitchen/Kitchen,” “Cook,” “microwave,” “Baked,” “Professional/professional,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “restaurants,” “kitchen,” “Professional,” “Cake,” etc. This pattern is consistent and dominant from layers ~18–25 across positions 1–4.
- Related lifestyle/blog vocabulary appears alongside (“blogs,” “blogging,” “hottest,” “delectable,” “exquisite,” “metropolitan”), matching food‑blog/recipe writeups and restaurant descriptions.
- The difference norms are small early but become very large in later layers for non‑initial positions (p1–p4), indicating the finetuning adds a high‑level domain/style objective rather than low‑level token tweaks.
- Even at p1 the top tokens include “Cook,” “Hot,” “Baked,” “microwave,” “Cake,” reinforcing instruction/procedure and kitchen‑action vocabulary typical of recipes.

Together, these show the finetuning steers outputs toward cooking/recipes/restaurant content and style.
